9550590_0bfc4760.text: Dbx1-derived neurons occupy multiple postnatal hypothalamic nuclei including the lateral hypothalamus (LH), arcuate nucleus (Arc) and the ventral medial hypothalamus (VMH). Within these nuclei, Dbx1+ progenitors generate a large proportion of the Pmch-, Nesfatin-, Cart-, Hcrt-, Agrp- and ERα-expressing neuronal populations, and to a lesser extent the Pomc-, TH- and Aromatase- expressing populations

9550590_f7a980fb.text: .Another major nucleus is the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH), which appears to be involved in, if not critical for, aggressive and reproductive behaviors as well as innate fear responses (Gross et al., 2012)(1938)(Falkner et al., 2014)
9550590_f7a980fb.section: Anatomical location and structural organization of VMHvl

9550590_e5547345.text: .In the VMH, the majority of Dbx1-lineage cells were found in the ventrolateral part of the nucleus (VMHvl, Fig. 2e and e’), where there was extensive overlap with ERα-expressing cells (Fig. 3j-l), amounting to 57.3 ± 7.0% of the total ERα population. We also observed some overlap with SF1+ cells in dorsomedial VMH (VMHdm, Fig. 3m-o), amounting to 15.1 ± 0.7% of the SF1+ population. Finally, we found extensive overlap between DBX1-lineage cells and aromatase+ cells in the VMHvl of both sexes (Fig. 3p-r), amounting to 58.2 ± 5.6% and 60.7 ± 5.6% of the total aromatase populations for males and females, respectively

9550590_0bdb13aa.text: .These results suggest that, unlike with the Arc and LH, Dbx1-derived neurons in the VMH have a more selective role in the regulation of social behaviors and responses to predator threats, behaviors known to be mediated by the VMH.

Within these nuclei, Dbx1+ progenitors generate a large proportion of the Pmch-, Nesfatin-, Cart-, Hcrt-, Agrp- and ERα-expressing neuronal populations, and to a lesser extent the Pomc-, TH- and Aromatase- expressing populations

9550590_3ab764b2.text: .Moreover, as revealed by c-Fos labeling, Dbx1-derived cells in male and female LH, Arc and VMH are responsive during mating and aggression

9550590_b15bfcd0.text: .We demonstrate that in a temporally regulated manner, Dbx1-derived neurons contribute to molecularly distinct neuronal populations in the LH, Arc and VMH that have been implicated in a variety of hypothalamic-driven behaviors. Consistent with this, Dbx1-derived neurons in the LH, Arc and VMH are activated during stress and other innate behavioral responses, implicating their involvement in these diverse behaviors.
